### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via createDispatcherPlugin (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via createDispatcherPlugin (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `15a24e056e376f827186a1ae6501f449bbec0aee` — the merge of head `49546b0c061e7fd4a65d125b67a1bc32aea7181c` into base `959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 15a24e056e376f827186a1ae6501f449bbec0aee && git checkout 15a24e056e376f827186a1ae6501f449bbec0aee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678 49546b0c061e7fd4a65d125b67a1bc32aea7181c && git checkout -B drift-repro 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678 && git merge --no-ff 49546b0c061e7fd4a65d125b67a1bc32aea7181c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `49546b0c061e7fd4a65d125b67a1bc32aea7181c`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, on 2026-10-08T04:25Z: card #22147 (body and all four comments — the ruling 6051299672, the claim, the os-dev-report, the seat's ACCEPT), PR #22177 (body, the 5-file list, the net diff `origin/main...49546b0c`; merge base `fec87e7e`, `origin/main` at `959c209d`), the 42 check-runs on the head, the #21908 and #22146 bodies, the code on `origin/main`, and the published `@objectstack/runtime` 17.7.0 tarball (sha1 matches the registry). The PR head had not moved. The seat's and the dev's conclusions were re-derived, not adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

**The falsified premise — confirmed on `origin/main`, independently.** The endpoint fallback (`createDispatcherPlugin`, `setFallbackHandler`) calls `HttpDispatcher.resolveRequestScope`, which assigns `context.executionContext` from `timedResolveExecutionContext` → `resolveExecutionContext` (`packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts`), whose return type is a Promise of `ExecutionContext` (never undefined) and whose last statement is `assembleExecutionContextOrGuest(...)`. In `packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts`, `entryFields(input, anonymous = true)` emits `positions: ['guest']`, `principalKind: 'guest'`, `isSystem: false`, and a `userId` of undefined that `emit` drops. The envelope then rides `protocolContext.executionContext` → `runAppEndpointStep` → `buildEndpointExecutionContext` → `executeObjectOperation`'s `deps.callData(..., ctx.executionContext)` and `executeFlow`'s `buildAutomationContext(ctx.body, ctx.protocolContext)`, which copies `positions` and, when present, `userId` off the envelope and never writes `isSystem`. The card's static reading ("threads `undefined` for anonymous") came from the JSDoc on `BuildEndpointExecutionContextInput.executionContext`, not from the code. **Right:** the PR builds no behaviour change; ruling C already holds at this door on `main`.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes implied by the diff: none.** File by file:
- `endpoint-executor.ts`, `api-endpoint-step.ts`: every changed line is inside the JSDoc of `BuildEndpointExecutionContextInput.executionContext` and `AppEndpointExecutionInput.executionContext`; the member declarations are byte-identical. **Right.** The new sentences are true of the normal path (③ names the one residual).
- `dispatcher-plugin.ts`: five `//` lines above the `resolveRequestScope` call inside `createDispatcherPlugin`'s body. **Right**, and "the ONE place the guest principal is built" is true of this door.
- No `packages/spec`, `packages/core`, `plugin-security`, `service-automation` or docs edit; the docs sentence in `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx` is already true of `main` and is not edited, as the card asked. **Right.** The Docs Drift Check lists two pages via the `createDispatcherPlugin` symbol; the diff changes a comment inside that function, so no page's accuracy moves. Advisory only.

**The pins — do they hold the ruled posture, and would each go red if it broke?** Card pin by card pin:
1. An anonymous `object_operation` reaches the engine as the guest, never principal-less — **held at two tiers.** Socket (`dispatcher-plugin.endpoint-fallback.integration.test.ts`, 4 new cases): the fixture stubs `auth`, `objectql` and `automation` at the KERNEL boundary (identity by a test header through the stubbed session getter), so the production `resolveRequestScope` → `resolveExecutionContext` → `assembleExecutionContextOrGuest` chain runs for real; the pin asserts the context the engine stub received is defined, matches `principalKind: 'guest'`, `positions: ['guest']`, `isSystem: false`, and carries no `userId`. Real boot (`declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest.dogfood.test.ts`, 6 new cases; `bootStack` with `automation: true` and a `MetadataPlugin`): an engine spy on `find` / `findOne` / `insert` captures the handed context, and a middleware registered after boot (so it runs last) records driver reach. Principal-less → the defined-context assertion reddens at both tiers, and on the real boot the deny would become a serve (the dev's A1 reading: 200 on find and get, 201 on create — the one check that still tells a guest from a principal-less call once #21908's deny makes both answer 403). System → `isSystem: false` reddens (A3). **Right.**
2. With no permission set bound to the guest, denied and nothing disclosed — **held** (dogfood): 403 with `error.code` `PERMISSION_DENIED`, no `data` member, neither the seeded row's marker nor its id anywhere in the response text, the driver never reached; for create, an admin read-back shows the seeded row and not the anonymous one. **Right.**
3. The same endpoint declared `authRequired: true` answers 401, unchanged — **held at both tiers**, with the engine never asked (the `authRequired` branch of `applyEndpointPolicies` in `endpoint-policy.ts` runs before delegation). A2 reddens it. **Right.**
4. `isSystem` never set on the anonymous path — **held for what this door hands down**: the object path (`isSystem: false` asserted) and the flow hand-off (no `isSystem` property; A4 reddens it, and `buildAutomationContext` on `main` never writes one). A flow's OWN declared `runAs: 'system'` elevating its data steps is a separate fact; see ③.
5. A `flow` endpoint's data calls carry the same guest context — **not landed as written, and correctly not claimed.** What is pinned: the flow EXECUTOR is handed `positions: ['guest']` with no `userId`, no `isSystem` and no `runAs`, and a `runAs: 'user'` run with no user is refused fail-closed before its data node touches the engine (400 `FLOW_FAILED`; engine and driver untouched; no disclosure). The data calls themselves either do not happen (`runAs: 'user'`) or run as the flow's declared system principal (`runAs: 'system'`), and `AutomationContext` (the spec contract) has no `principalKind` or `isSystem` member, so the guest reaches a flow as a position only. The PR says so, routes it (③), and is `Part of`, not `Fixes`, so merging does not close the card over an unlanded pin. **Right.**
Also pinned: an authenticated request at `authRequired: false` runs as that user (`principalKind: 'human'`, no `guest` position; A5 reddens it). **Right** — it guards the opposite failure, a guest everywhere.

**Public text at class level.** The PR body, the os-dev-report and the ACCEPT describe reach by class (door, gate, driver, status) with no request shape against a shipped endpoint; the ablation readings describe a mutated build, not `main`. The two test files exercise inline, throwaway fixtures (a test-only object and namespace in a stack the test itself declares), which is what a pin is; nothing in them reaches a real deployment's data. The throwaway probe is not in the diff (5 files, as listed). **Right.**

**Check-runs on `49546b0c`, read 2026-10-08T04:25Z:** 42 runs — 28 success, 11 skipped, 1 failure, 2 in progress (`Test Core (1/6)`, `Lint & Repo Gates`). Green and complete: `Build Core`; `Test Core (2/6)` through `(6/6)`; `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards; `Dogfood Verify CLI`; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`; the four `Type Check` rows and `TypeScript Type Check`; `Spec property liveness`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`; `Part-of PR must not also close its card`; `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`; both single-writer guards; `Check Documentation Links`; `Flag docs affected by code changes`. The one failure is `Check Changeset` at 04:12:24Z, before `skip-changeset` was applied (04:17Z); the two `labeled` runs of that job at 04:17:49Z and 04:17:50Z are `skipped` by the job's own `if:` (the payload carries the label), which the workflow documents as the exemption. Recorded as read; the two in-progress rows are the seat's to see complete before the queue.

### ② Semver level

**`skip-changeset` is right, and `Clause-②: no` with no arm is right.**
- `@objectstack/runtime` publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only (`files`); `tsup` bundles from `src/index.ts`, which exports nothing from `api-endpoint-step.ts`, `endpoint-executor.ts` or `endpoint-policy.ts` (read on `origin/main`). Verified against the published 17.7.0 tarball (sha1 `8f079ab4…` matches the registry; `main` is at 17.7.0): neither `BuildEndpointExecutionContextInput` nor `AppEndpointExecutionInput` appears anywhere under `dist/`; the pre-existing `#4936` comment beside the `resolveRequestScope` call is absent from `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs` (esbuild strips non-legal comments); the control, `createDispatcherPlugin`, is present in all four bundles. The one hit for the phrase "undefined for anonymous" in the d.ts belongs to `resolveActiveOrganizationId` on the domain-handler registry — a different declaration this diff does not touch — so the seat's "the old text of all three comments is absent" holds for the three comments in question. The diff adds no export, so the new text is unreachable the same way.
- The two test files do not ship (`files` excludes `src`), and `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`.
- Nothing changed for anonymous endpoints, so there is no release note to write; a `patch` entry would describe a change that did not happen. AGENTS.md's criterion for the label ("a diff that publishes nothing from any released package") is met exactly. The dispatch's `patch` ask was premised on a code change that proved unnecessary, and the departure is on the record in the PR body, the os-dev-report (open question 2) and the ACCEPT.
- `Clause-②: no` is PR line 2. **Right**: no accepted input or published shape moves. The card's anticipated `(narrowing)` arm is correctly dropped — nothing narrows, because the anonymous call was never handed through principal-less at this door.
- `.changeset/`: none on the head (the second commit removed the one the first added). Consistent with the label.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry, judged:
1. **Open question 1 — a flow declaring `runAs: 'system'` under an anonymous `authRequired: false` request.** Measured by the dev and consistent with `domains/automation.ts` on `main` ("the engine elevates to a system principal only when the flow declares `runAs: 'system'`"): the request arrives as the guest; the elevation is the flow author's declaration. Whether ruling C's "never the system principal" reaches a flow's own `runAs` is a maintainer ruling, not a seat's; the seat **escalates** (card to `needs-user-decision` at landing with the dev's four options and recommendation A, and a pointer to #22146 question 2). **Right.** The PR builds nothing for it and does not close the card. For the ruling: the docs' own anonymous example is a flow, and until a guest grants channel exists an elevated flow is the only way an anonymous flow can touch data, so option C or D taken now would be reshaped by #22146.
2. **Open question 2 — changeset:** answered in ②. **Right.**
3. **Open question 3 — #21908's `Blocked-by: #22147`:** B, keep #21908 blocked until this PR merges. **Right**: once the engine-level deny lands, a guest and a principal-less call both answer 403 and only these pins tell them apart, so the pins must be on `main` first. #21908's pointer comment already names #22147 as the gate; lifting the line is its owner's call, as the seat says.
4. **Dev flag — the identity-resolution fault path.** Confirmed in `HttpDispatcher.resolveRequestScope`: the `catch` calls `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` and otherwise leaves `executionContext` undefined, and the fallback branch then spreads nothing into `execution.executionContext`, so at an `authRequired: false` endpoint such a call would run principal-less through the ADR-0096 E1 hand-off. Independent read of the anonymous branch: the session getter and the OAuth verification each absorb their own faults; `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` re-raises unbranded faults as the loud class; the only `throw` in `resolveAuthzContext` is `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`; `getQl` guards its first lookup. No fault a request can steer was found; what remains is an infrastructure fault class. The pins cannot cover it (it needs a fault injection), so the ruled "never principal-less" is held on the request-steerable path rather than by construction, and the two corrected comments' "never `undefined`" is true of that path only. The seat **routes** it to #21908 at landing, whose engine-level deny closes it by construction and which waits on this PR. **Right**, with one note for the seat: the dispatch's suggested consumer-side guard in the fallback branch (inside this claim's file surface) would have closed it at the door as well; the dev's reason for declining — a second guest construction for a value never undefined on the normal path — stands, and the routing keeps the closure where #21908 owns it.
5. **Dev flag — `AutomationContext` has no `principalKind` or `isSystem`**, so a guest-triggered flow sees only the `guest` position, and `resolveRunDataContext` refuses a user-less `runAs: 'user'` run rather than running it as the guest. A `packages/spec` change, out of this card's scope; **routed** to #22146. **Right.**
6. **Deviations:** `Part of` rather than `Fixes` — **right** (the card keeps an open ruling; the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` check is green). No production change and the suggested route not taken — **right**, verified in ①. No changeset — ②. Model-free commit trailers per AGENTS.md — not a contract matter. A4's void first attempt redone — reported, and the socket pin's missing-`isSystem` assertion is the one it reddens. Throwaway probe never committed — verified from the file list.
7. **The seat's own pending items** — its `dispatch-gates --self-test` at the head, the `mkdtempSync` standing-lesson note, and the two in-progress check-runs — are the seat's to read before the queue; nothing in this verdict depends on them.

No flag is unanswered or unrouted. No pin asserts a request a reader could reuse against a deployment.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22147-anonymous-endpoint-guest`
Reviewed-by: `session_01RWZbGvPFcRKvUqASZtunCU`

**VERDICT: PASS**
